paper_metadata.title: Prognosis of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy 45 years after onset: Seizure outcome and predictors

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population and inclusion criteria. However, the sample is a hospital-based cohort treated by a single specialist, which the authors admit may lead to selection bias toward more motivated and compliant patients with higher socioeconomic status.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The records of the 339 patients with IGE showed that 82 patients had been diagnosed with JME; 190 had absence epilepsy, 51 had GTCS on awakening, and 16 had unclassifiable generalized epilepsy.
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the larger IGE cohort from which the JME patients were derived.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: All included patients were diagnosed and treated by the same doctor, a senior epileptologist and one of the authors (D.J.).
items.reasoning: While the recruitment from a specific clinic is clear, the 'single-doctor' nature introduces potential referral bias and limits generalizability.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: last patient contact (personally or via telephone interview between January and July 2011).
items.reasoning: The final contact period is defined, and the retrospective nature implies recruitment over the decades of the senior author's practice.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: treated at the Department of Neurology, Charité–Universitätsmedizin Berlin
items.reasoning: The specific academic medical center and department are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We included patients who had been diagnosed with JME according to the classification of the International League Against Epilepsy (1989) and had been followed up for at least 20 years.
items.reasoning: Standard ILAE criteria and a specific minimum follow-up duration were used.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of 82 patients with a diagnosis of JME, sufficient information on seizure outcome was available for 66 patients... indicating a recruitment rate of more than 80%.
items.reasoning: A participation rate of >80% is generally considered low risk for selection bias.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical data for all patients included in the study are presented in table 1.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides age at onset, sex, EEG findings, and presence of absence seizures.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for the 16 excluded patients and demonstrates that they did not differ significantly from the included cohort, minimizing the risk of attrition bias.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: 66 patients finally included... recruitment rate of more than 80%.
items.reasoning: The majority of the identified cohort was successfully followed up.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Sixteen patients who were excluded from the study did not differ significantly from the final study population regarding age at epilepsy onset and at investigation, sex, and occurrence of absence seizures
items.reasoning: The authors performed a sensitivity analysis comparing excluded and included patients.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 8 because of insufficient documentation of data and another 8 because of loss to follow-up.
items.reasoning: Specific reasons for exclusion from the final analysis are provided.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: did not differ significantly... regarding age at epilepsy onset and at investigation, sex, and occurrence of absence seizures
items.reasoning: Key prognostic factors were compared between the groups.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Sixteen patients who were excluded from the study did not differ significantly from the final study population
items.reasoning: Statistical comparison confirmed no significant differences.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors were based on clinical records and standardized EEG, which are standard in epilepsy research. The primary predictor (absence seizures) is a well-defined clinical event.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Potential predictors of seizure outcome assessed in this study were age at onset of JME, genetic traits... first interictal EEG... appearance of absence seizures, sex, and insurance status
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly listed and defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All included patients were diagnosed and treated by the same doctor, a senior epileptologist
items.reasoning: Consistency in measurement is high due to the single-expert diagnosis, though recall bias is a factor for historical seizure types.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Age at onset, y, mean 6 SD 14.3 6 4.1
items.reasoning: Continuous variables like age and follow-up time are reported as means/SDs.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patient data were analyzed based on the case records and via direct contact by telephone and/or postal letter.
items.reasoning: A standardized protocol (structured questionnaire and record review) was used for all.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 82 patients had been diagnosed with JME... 8 because of insufficient documentation of data
items.reasoning: Patients with missing data were excluded, and the remaining 66 had complete profiles.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study did not use imputation; it excluded cases with insufficient data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) is clearly defined, but its measurement relies heavily on patient self-report (recall) over a very long period, which is susceptible to bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: 5-year terminal remission... defined as the time between onset of JME... and last patient contact
items.reasoning: The primary outcome is explicitly defined as 5 years of seizure freedom at the end of follow-up.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Each patient was asked to answer a structured questionnaire regarding seizures and treatment. Forty-six patients answered directly by telephone or by returning the questionnaire.
items.reasoning: Self-reporting is standard for long-term epilepsy follow-up but lacks objective verification (e.g., video-EEG) for the terminal period.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patient data were analyzed based on the case records and via direct contact by telephone and/or postal letter.
items.reasoning: The same structured questionnaire approach was applied to the cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study identifies a key predictor but relies on univariate analyses (Fisher exact, ANOVA). While they mention 'independent predictor' in the abstract, the statistical section does not describe a multivariable model to adjust for all confounders simultaneously.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Potential predictors... age at onset, genetic traits, first interictal EEG... sex, and insurance status.
items.reasoning: Key clinical and demographic variables were collected.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 Summary of clinical data

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders

items.evidence_snippet: All included patients were diagnosed and treated by the same doctor
items.reasoning: Clinical records from a single expert provide high internal reliability for confounder measurement.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patient data were analyzed based on the case records and via direct contact
items.reasoning: Standardized data collection was used.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study did not use matching or stratification in the design phase.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: For comparison of patients with 5-year terminal remission and those without, Fisher exact test was used for categorical dependent variables, and univariate analysis of variance was used for metric-dependent variables.
items.reasoning: The analysis is primarily univariate. There is no evidence of a multivariable logistic regression to adjust for confounding.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the sample size and the descriptive nature of the study. Results are reported transparently, including effect sizes.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Data were analyzed using SPSS version 18.0 software... Fisher exact test was used... univariate analysis of variance was used
items.reasoning: The statistical plan is clearly laid out.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Comparison of clinical variables as potential predictors of seizure outcome
items.reasoning: The study tests specific clinical hypotheses but lacks a complex multivariable model building strategy.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test revealed that all metric variables were normally distributed... variances were homogeneous
items.reasoning: The authors verified the assumptions for the statistical tests used.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: All clinical variables of seizure outcome are presented in table 2.
items.reasoning: The study reports on all potential predictors mentioned in the methods, including non-significant ones.
